evidence.detail: 30.cli-interface.srs.md:7072 (IR-CLI-113 AC-2) now derives `sent`, `waived`, `failed`, `interrupted` and `pending` from the journal alone "as FR-NODE-251 AC-3 derives them ... whether or not the citation scan ran", and without the scan lists in `attention[]` only failed/blocked nodes and nodes holding failed/interrupted actions. :7074 (AC-4) emits `due` and `held-unverified` only with `--with-tests`, splitting `pending` by FR-NODE-251 AC-4 so their sum equals `pending`; :7077 (AC-7) requires those counts to equal `wave actions` for the same inputs. 50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md:16718 (FR-NODE-249 AC-2) says only a state computed with the scan decides due vs held-unverified; :16859-16860 (FR-NODE-251 AC-3, AC-4) use the same name `held-unverified`. Iter-2 counter-case re-run: complete node, ACs checked/covered/unexpired, one uncited, one notify with no journal line -> `wave status` without the scan: node `done`, action_counts {pending: 1}, no due/held-unverified key; with `--with-tests`: node `unverified`, {pending: 1, due: 0, held-unverified: 1}; `wave actions`: held-unverified. findings.description: The status/actions state split is closed: unscanned counts stop at `pending`, scanned counts split it the way `wave actions` does, and both requirements use `held-unverified`.
